summary: Crow's nest on Sky Hill (Kootenai Co., ID) in 1934, abandoned 1935; an undated hiking guide found no sign of a camp or observation tree on the ridge.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1935. A hiking guide searched the summit ridge for a camp or observation tree and found nothing; no source describes a footing or structure on the summit today.

access.note: The route crosses private timberland under an agreement allowing non-motorized public access, so the summit is reached only on those terms. The summit sits on National Forest land.

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 miles of hiking and 1,000 feet of climb from the pass on Skygazer Lane.

events.note: Crow's nest in place on the ridge

evidence.supports: About three miles north of Harrison

evidence.quote: In 1934 there was a crows nest. It was abandoned in 1935 (Kresek).

evidence.supports: Hiker searched the ridge for a camp or observation tree
evidence.quote: I searched all along the ridge for any signs of a camp or tree used for observation.

evidence.supports: Isolated parcel of National Forest land
evidence.quote: Located on an isolated parcel of National Forest land

evidence.supports: Route crosses private timberland under non-motorized access agreement
evidence.quote: The route starts with private timberlands but they have an agreement for non-motorized access with the public.

evidence.supports: Access from the pass on Skygazer Lane
evidence.quote: Access is best from the pass on Skygazer Lane.

notes_for_editor: Kind platform is correct: structure_kinds says crow's nests count as platforms when a source calls them crow's nests, and FFLA's Crowsnest label agrees. Location conflict left open: record uses FFLA 47.50642, -116.7729; idaho_fl has 47.49963, -116.7896, about 1.46 km apart. I could not check either pair against the text (firelookout.com gives 3 miles north of Harrison). Elevation 3650 ft per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; no elevation key in the schema, so not stored. The access level restricted is my reading of WillhiteWeb's access note; please confirm before publishing. The same WillhiteWeb page also says a motorcycle trail runs straight up the ridge from the pass, which sits oddly with the non-motorized agreement; the story therefore gives no access advice. Harrison is sourced to firelookout.com only; the Idaho Fire Lookouts and weebly pages do not name it. WillhiteWeb is undated, so the search date is unknown and the research summary avoids a year for it. Dates rest on four sources that agree.
